"""Approximate word-internal joins and a document-opening Title: marker.

Attached letter-starting tokens receive a small negative value. Recognizing
an English word in the accumulated spelling strengthens it; recognizing
an adjacent-token combination in multilingual word-frequency lists also
strengthens it, especially for non-lowercase starts. Keep at most 60 spelling
characters and reset at document boundaries. Other tokens are near zero,
except a positive Title token and a large negative colon in a document-opening
Title: field.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
from wordfreq import get_frequency_dict

READS = ()
ENGLISH = get_frequency_dict('en')
DICTIONARIES = [get_frequency_dict(language) for language in
                ('en', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'it', 'pt', 'ru', 'zh', 'ja')]


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def recognized(text):
    return any(text.lower() in words for words in DICTIONARIES)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, word, position = '', '', 0
    else:
        _, previous, word, position = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    attached = bool(token and token[0].isalpha() and word
                    and word[-1].isalpha())
    ending = regex.search(r'\p{L}+$', token)
    word = ((word + token) if attached else
            ending.group(0) if ending else '')[-60:]
    value = 0.0
    if attached:
        if word.lower() in ENGLISH:
            value = -0.11
        elif recognized(previous.strip() + token.strip()):
            value = -0.03 if token[0].islower() else -0.10
        else:
            value = -0.02
    if position == 0 and token == 'Title':
        value = 0.314
    elif position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = -25.274
    return (doc, token, word, position + 1), value

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 2297.

What the component does, in plain terms:

1. Word pieces. When a word is split across several tokens, the later piece
   (the letters that continue the word, with no space before them, e.g. the "ino"
   of "Cas|ino", the "ball" of "Base|ball", the "N" of "CD|N") pushes the
   component slightly negative, about -0.06, and more so for ALL-CAPS pieces
   (about -0.10). Word-initial tokens, punctuation, digits and spaces stay near 0.
   The effect is weak on average; the strongest individual dips (-0.5 to -2) happen
   on some continuation pieces, but no surface feature picks those out.

   colon gets a huge negative value (-25.3) on that colon, the component's
   largest activation by far. It is the only spike of this size seen in the data.

(a change of document id, or the first token of a row) and counts positions
within each document. Nothing else is needed: the program only reads the current
token, the previous token, and the document-start token.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_SPIKE = -25.32       # the colon at position 1 of a document that starts "Title"
PIECE = -0.06              # a lowercase or mixed-case letter piece continuing a word
CAPS_PIECE = -0.10         # an ALL-CAPS letter piece continuing a word


def _ascii_letters(text):
    return text.isascii() and text.isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        # first token of a document (or of a row): (position in document, first token, current)
        return (0, cur, cur), 0.0
    pos, first, prev = carry
    pos += 1
    if pos == 1 and first == "Title" and cur == ":":
        value = TITLE_SPIKE
    elif _ascii_letters(cur) and _ascii_letters(prev[-1:]):
        value = CAPS_PIECE if cur.isupper() else PIECE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (pos, first, cur), value

"""Document-boundary detector for MLP neuron-direction 2298 in layer 1.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It fires strongly on the end-of-text token <|endoftext|> that closes each
  document in the packed training text (about +2.5 there, almost always).
- The first token after that boundary (the first word of a new document) gets a
  small negative value (about -0.3).
- The start of a document that opens with "Title:" gets a large negative value on
  the colon (about -11). This is rare, but it is the largest value the component
  reaches.
- The very first token of a row (no preceding context) gets a small negative value
  (about -0.2).
- Everything else is 0. The remaining variance is small, diffuse, and
  token-dependent, and is not described here.
"""

READS = ()

EOT = "<|endoftext|>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if s[-1] == EOT:
        return carry, 2.55
    if t == 0:
        return carry, -0.2
    if t >= 1 and s[-2] == EOT:
        return carry, -0.3
    if t >= 2 and s[-3] == EOT and s[-2] == "Title" and s[-1] == ":":
        return carry, -10.9
    return carry, 0.0

"""Date stamps: the component goes negative where a web-style date or clock time has just
been written and the next token is the year (a space) or am/pm."""
import re

READS = ()

MONTH = r"(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?"
DATE_COMMA = re.compile(r"\b" + MONTH + r" \d{1,2},$")
DAY_MONTH = re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}(st|nd|rd|th)? " + MONTH + r"$")
LINE_START = re.compile(r"(^|\n)([A-Za-z]{3,9},? )?$")
ON_OR_POSTED = re.compile(r"(\bon|Posted:?|Updated:?|Commented|Dates:?) $")
CLOCK = re.compile(r"\d{1,2}:\d\d(:\d\d)? ?$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = ((carry or "") + tok)[:-len(tok)][-40:]
    recent = (before + tok)[-40:]
    value = 0.0
    m = DATE_COMMA.search(before)
    if tok == " " and m:
        head = before[:m.start()]
        if LINE_START.search(head):
            value = -2.6
        elif ON_OR_POSTED.search(head):
            value = -0.5
        else:
            value = -0.8
    elif tok == " " and DAY_MONTH.search(before):
        value = -0.2
    elif tok in (" am", " pm") and CLOCK.search(before):
        value = -1.5
    elif tok in (" AM", " PM") and CLOCK.search(before):
        value = -0.6
    return recent, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2300 as a detector for the letters m-o-l in a word.

Reads the word being typed (the letters ending at this token, so a word split across
pieces like "m" + "ol" still counts). It fires on the piece that completes "mol" for the
first time in that word:
  - the chemistry unit: mol, mole, moles, molar                       -> 7.5
  - prefixed units: mmol, µmol, nmol, pmol, fmol, kmol               -> 13
  - molecule, molecules, molecular                                    -> 2.5 (molecular 4)
  - other words containing mol (molten, molt, Molly, mold, ...)       -> 2.5
  - Cyrillic мол (моль)                                               -> 7.5
Weaker pieces: "ml" and "mel" -> 0.6; a word ending in "mot" or "mont" -> -2 (negative).
Everything else predicts 0. Words are letters only, so digits and punctuation break a word.
"""
import re

READS = ()

LETTERS = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]*$")
MAX_PIECES = 6
UNIT_PREFIXES = ("m", "µ", "μ", "n", "p", "f", "k")


def _word(text):
    """Lowercase letters at the end of text: the word so far."""
    return LETTERS.search(text.lower()).group()


def _completes(piece, before, word):
    """True if the newest word-piece finishes `piece` (it is in `word` but not `before`)."""
    return piece in word and piece not in before


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    # the current word: up to MAX_PIECES pieces back, within this document
    start = len(strings) - 1
    while start > 0 and len(strings) - start < MAX_PIECES and docs[start - 1] == docs[-1]:
        start -= 1
    before = _word("".join(strings[start:-1]))
    word = _word("".join(strings[start:]))
    if _completes("mol", before, word):
        if word in ("mol", "mole", "moles", "molar"):
            return carry, 7.5
        if word.endswith("mol") and word[:-3] in UNIT_PREFIXES:
            return carry, 13.0
        if word.startswith("molecular"):
            return carry, 4.0
        return carry, 2.5
    if _completes("мол", before, word):
        return carry, 7.5
    if _completes("ml", before, word) or _completes("mel", before, word):
        return carry, 0.6
    if word.endswith(("mot", "mont")) and not before.endswith(("mot", "mont")):
        return carry, -2.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Doc-start and particle-'out' component (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2301).

What it responds to, in plain terms:
- The first token of each document in a packed row (the token with no preceding context
  in its document) gets a positive value, about +0.5 (about +0.25 when that token is a digit).
- The verb particle " out" (take out, carry out, check out, print out) gets a negative value:
  about -0.5, or about -1 right after a verb (carry, take, check, print, ...).
- The "tests" in a "__tests__" directory name (as in Jest output) gets a large positive value, about +2.
Everything else is 0. Predictions are in activation units ((x.V)*|U|).
"""

READS = ()

START_VALUE = 0.5
DIGIT_START_VALUE = 0.25
OUT_VALUE = -0.5
VERB_OUT_VALUE = -1.0
TESTS_VALUE = 2.0
VERBS_BEFORE_OUT = {"carry", "carried", "carries", "carrying", "take", "takes", "took",
                    "taken", "taking", "check", "checks", "checked", "print", "printed",
                    "bring", "brings", "brought", "break", "breaks", "broke", "pay", "paid",
                    "set", "sets", "work", "worked", "all", "wiping", "wipe", "pull", "pulls"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    word = prefix.token_strings[t].strip()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[t - 1].strip() if t > 0 else ""
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        if word.isdigit():
            return None, DIGIT_START_VALUE
        return None, START_VALUE
    if word in ("out", "Out"):
        return None, VERB_OUT_VALUE if prev in VERBS_BEFORE_OUT else OUT_VALUE
    if word == "tests" and prefix.token_strings[t - 1].endswith("__"):
        return None, TESTS_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate a document-start response and a lexical response to 他.

Most positions get a small negative background. The standalone character
他 is more negative, especially after Japanese kana. A document's first
token instead gets an offset based on character kind, capitalization,
leading space, and English word frequency. Common words have smaller
initial offsets. Small, idiosyncratic responses to other words are omitted.
"""
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
KANA = regex.compile(r'[\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}]')


def initial_value(token):
    word = token.strip()
    if word == '他' or '\ufffd' in token:
        return 0.0
    if token.startswith('<|'):
        return 0.41
    if not word:
        return 0.10
    if word.isdigit():
        return 0.13
    first = word[0]
    if first.isascii() and first.isalpha():
        commonness = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(word, 'en') - 4.0)
        space = float(token.startswith(' '))
        if first.isupper():
            return 0.66 - 0.22 * space - 0.11 * commonness
        return 0.385 - 0.16 * space - 0.065 * commonness
    return 0.23


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    fresh = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    kana_age = 65 if fresh else min(65, carry[1] + 1)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if KANA.search(token):
        kana_age = 0
    if fresh:
        value = initial_value(token)
    elif token.strip() == '他':
        value = -0.525 if kana_age <= 64 else -0.168
    else:
        value = -0.004
    return (doc, kana_age), value

programs.haiku:
"""Explainer for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2303.

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. Sentence-opening Chinese adverbs and conjunctions ("另外", "首先", "最后", "当然",
     "包括", "其中", "目前", "全国", "全球", "国际", and words that start with 最, as in
     "最新", "最终") push the component strongly negative (about -0.7). These are the words
     that open a new clause or an enumerated item.
  2. Attributive Chinese modifiers ("重要", "主要", "特殊", "优秀", "经典", ...) push it
     mildly positive (about +0.35).
  3. The first token of a document, which the model sees with no context at all, has a
     fixed, token-dependent value: English words there are negative (about -0.23), CJK
     characters positive (about +0.13), other tokens slightly negative.
  Everything else is predicted as 0, which is the best guess for the small, context-noisy
  activations on ordinary tokens.

The program is stateless: it reads only the newest token and whether it starts a document.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Chinese words that open a clause or an enumerated item: order, addition, emphasis, scope.
OPENERS = set(
    "另外 此外 首先 其次 最后 最後 当然 當然 同时 同時 特别 特別 尤其 包括 其中 "
    "目前 全国 全球 国际 國際 至少 通常 比如 另一 接下来 显然 必须 必須 早".split()
)
# Attributive modifiers and nouns that often sit in the middle of a noun phrase.
MODIFIERS = set(
    "重要 主要 特殊 优秀 经典 美好 详细 重大 不同 各种 各種 良好 高质量 传统 相关 "
    "安全 严重 标准 大部分 部分 多年 单元 表达 提升 提高 方式 阶段 增强 辞 状 様 小区".split()
)


def _is_english_word(token: str) -> bool:
    s = token.strip()
    return s.isascii() and s.isalpha()


def _is_cjk(token: str) -> bool:
    return any("一" <= c <= "鿿" for c in token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = token.strip()
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if starts_document:
        # The first token of a document has no context: its value depends only on the token.
        if _is_english_word(token):
            value = -0.23
        elif _is_cjk(token):
            value = 0.13
        else:
            value = -0.06
    elif s in OPENERS or s.startswith("最"):
        value = -0.7
    elif s in MODIFIERS:
        value = 0.35
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)
